title: Domain object
description:
One construct of a domain analysis, stored in the knowledge notation. The vocabulary is the eight kinds the analysis records, 1:1 with them: nothing is collapsed into a field of something else, so every construct keeps an identifier and a file. The envelope is `schemas/knowledge-notation.json`'s and is carried rather than decided here.

What this contract adds to the notation is per-kind content and the alternation over it: a node declares everything its kind requires, or declares a gap naming that field. A non-empty `gaps` is the node's incompleteness — there is no status, no maturity level and no flag saying which pass has run, because an open `kind: authoring` gap already says it.

**Generated.** This document is composed from `domain/` and is not edited: every assertion in it is stated once, in the file of the table or the kind that owns it. See `domain/domain-graph.json`.

contract_version.description: A consumer rejects an artifact it was not built to read rather than inferring version from shape.

rationale.description: Why the analysis decided this, required wherever `origin` is `modeled`. A reviewer accepts a fact the material stated and disagrees with one the analysis reached, and can do the second only against a reason.

attributes.description: What this definition holds, fully typed against the closed primitive vocabulary. Where the material does not state a length or a precision, the parameter is left absent and a gap names it — see `../tables/primitives.json#/x-unstated-parameter`. Absent and unnamed is not the same statement, and only the second is refused.

consistency.description: Whether this rule holds inside one transaction or converges after it. Required of a rule that reaches outside its own aggregate, which no single file can see — `src/claude/bin/check_knowledge.py` decides it.

context_relationships.description: How this context relates to another. Authored edge, traversed only when expansion crosses a context.

allOf.description: A directional pattern names which side this context is on; a symmetric one has no side to name.

examples.description: Given/when/then cases a conformance test is derived from. Carried when `expression` is absent, and permitted alongside it. Where the material gives cases, both sides of the condition are recorded — a case that holds and a case that does not.

expression.description: The rule stated so a consumer can evaluate it. The grammar is deferred: it must be closed, total, side-effect free, and restricted to attributes reachable from the rule's boundary, and it arrives with the first consumer that evaluates one.

identity.description: Which attributes form this definition's identity. `strategy` inherits the base's declared default and is stated only where this definition differs.

initial.description: The state an instance starts in. Every state is reachable from it.

payload.description: The definition that gives this interface its shape. One home for the payload's type, in the same vocabulary every other typed thing uses — an event whose fields live only in an external file is a contract the graph cannot read. `schema` still points at the wire contract, which is stack knowledge.

rejections.description: The decided non-transitions. Two shorthands keep the declaration from becoming padding: a trigger list expands to one entry per trigger, and `from: terminal` expands to every state listed as terminal. Both are expanded before totality is checked.

from.description: A declared state, or the reserved name `terminal`.

error.description: The domain error this rejection raises, recorded as a definition whose ddd is domain-error.

root.description: The definition that is this aggregate's entry point. Exactly one, and its identity is the aggregate's.

schema.description: Where the machine-readable payload contract lives. The form of this value is not closed.

statement.description: The rule in prose, non-generative, and never the only place a fact a machine reads appears.

states.description: The legal states. Two is the minimum that makes a transition table meaningful. `terminal` is reserved as a rejection shorthand and is never a state name.

steps.description: The ordered steps, each naming exactly one node.

compensated_by.description: What undoes this step when a later one fails. A saga is defined by its compensations, and a step carrying only an identifier cannot hold one — so `saga` named a construct the structure could not represent.

subdomain.description: The subdomain this context partitions. Exactly one; the classification lives on the subdomain rather than being copied here.

subject.description: The definition whose states this governs. Exactly one, and at most one lifecycle per definition.

terminal.description: The states that accept no further trigger, declared rather than inferred, and expanded wherever a rejection names the reserved `terminal`.

transitions.description: The legal moves. Every non-terminal state has an outgoing transition.

guard.description: The rule that decides this transition, at most one.

emits.description: The events this transition raises. A state change that publishes a domain event is the core of an event-driven model, and with no edge for it the fact lands in the body — which is where a relationship stops being in the graph. A list because one move may raise more than one, and absent where it raises none.

upstream.description: The published interface this one consumes. A consumed interface is a local record of somebody else's contract, so without this the graph holds two nodes for one contract and cannot tell they are the same one. The consumer declares it; the publisher never enumerates who depends on it, for the reason a scope never enumerates what it holds.

allOf.description: A message or a shared vocabulary carries a shape. An `api` is an exposed operation and names none here.
Only a consumed interface names what it consumes. `upstream` on a published one would say this context both owns the contract and depends on someone else's.

schema.description: Where the machine-readable payload contract lives. The form of this value is not closed.

compensated_by.description: What undoes this step when a later one fails. A saga is defined by its compensations, and a step carrying only an identifier cannot hold one — so `saga` named a construct the structure could not represent.

then.description: A lifecycle-bound enum keeps the state set in one authority. A free enum lists its own values.

binding.description: A reference whose target lies in another aggregate declares `by-identity`. How a binding becomes a storage representation is stack knowledge and is not recorded.

boundaryId.description: The two scopes a node may belong to: a context is `dm.context.<context>`, an aggregate inside one is `dm.aggregate.<context>.<aggregate>`. Written as two patterns rather than one with an optional tail, because the optional tail applies to both alternatives and so admits `dm.context.<a>.<b>` and `dm.aggregate.<a>` — neither of which is a scope this profile holds. `domain-object/1` carries the single-pattern form and admits both.

consistency.description: Whether this rule holds within one transaction or converges after it. An invariant spanning two aggregates is eventually consistent, and saying so is the difference between a boundary drawn honestly and one drawn wide enough to hide the question.

contextRelationshipPattern.description: `separate-ways` is a real answer: two contexts that do not need each other are not connected because a diagram looks better connected. Four of the seven are directional and carry a `role`; three are symmetric and refuse one.

interfaceDdd.description: A `command` is a message a context accepts, and it belongs here because an interface is what a context publishes or consumes. `ownership: consumed` on a command says this context accepts it; `published` says this context sends it to another. A command that is refused never becomes a process, which is why it is not a `processDdd`.

interfaceId.description: An interface. Named by `payload`'s origin, by `transitions[].emits` and by `upstream`, which is why it needs a form of its own rather than being reached through `nodeId`.

kind.description: Closed at eight and 1:1 with the construct vocabulary the analysis records. Nothing is a field of something else, so nothing loses an identifier by being one.

nodeId.description: Any node of this profile. `dm.<kind>.<scope>.<slug>`, with `subdomain` and `context` taking `dm.<kind>.<slug>` because each is itself a scope.

ownership.description: Whether this context exposes the interface or depends on someone else's. It decides who owes whom compatibility.

relationshipRole.description: What *this* context is relative to the one it names. Upstream decides and owes compatibility; downstream absorbs the decision. Carried only by a directional pattern: a `shared-kernel` has no upstream side, and a `role` beside one would name a fact that does not exist.

slug.description: A name reduced to kebab-case. A name that will not reduce is a refusal rather than a transliteration: stripping an accent takes a rule no specification states, and the same name would reduce differently next time.

stateName.description: A lifecycle state. `terminal` is reserved as a rejection shorthand and is refused as a state name by the validator, which can see the whole state list; the pattern cannot express the reservation.

subdomainType.description: Where the business differs, where it is merely specific, and where the problem is solved. It decides where careful modelling is worth its cost.
